subject: KMS operational controls questionnaire — HSM/BYOK, rotation, and TLS
body:
From: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@finitybank.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@thirdlane.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KMS operational controls questions for Finity RFP

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the RFP. A couple of detail items came up from our crypto team as they're mapping your answers into our control matrix — could you confirm the following in writing?

1) For hosted Redwoods API customers, what parts of the key lifecycle are controlled by Redwood vs. the customer when BYOK is requested? Can you describe key import, storage (HSM or software), and whether you perform key wrapping with a root key under your control?

2) Which HSM vendors / certifications do you rely on for (a) Hosted, (b) Dedicated, and (c) Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments? We need explicit mention of FIPS / Common Criteria levels where available.

3) Rotation policy: what defaults do you enforce (data encryption key rotation, CMK rotation), and do you support customer-driven rotation schedules and cryptoperiods?

4) Backup/encryption-at-rest: are EBS/snapshots/backups encrypted with the same CMK? Are backup keys stored distinctly?

5) TLS policy: minimum TLS version supported for all endpoints (API, admin, inter-node), ciphers, and whether mutual TLS is available for Dedicated/Private control planes.

If you can provide a short one-page ops summary and any attestation docs we can circulate, that would be ideal.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Chow
Senior Information Security Manager — Finity Bank

Subject: Re: KMS operational controls questions for Finity RFP

Hi Elaine — thanks for the concise list. Below are direct answers; attaching a one-page ops summary and our latest FIPS/HSM attestation PDF for your review (redwood-kms-ops-2026.pdf, fips-attestation-2025.pdf). I also included a high-level dataflow diagram (dataflow-diagram.png).

1) BYOK model (Hosted API):
- Customer supplies a Customer Master Key (CMK) by either: (a) importing into Redwood's HSM-backed KMS via a secure PKCS#11 import flow, or (b) registering an external KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS) and providing an ARN/endpoint for envelope-wrapping.
- For imported CMKs on Hosted, keys are stored in an HSM-backed module (AWS CloudHSM or equivalent) and never exported in plaintext. We use an envelope key under Redwood control for service-side wrapping of ephemeral data keys; when customers use external KMS, Redwood does not hold the unwrapped CMK.
- For Dedicated and Private, customers always have the option to bring their own HSM (BYOK with customer-controlled HSM) or use Redwood-managed HSMs within their dedicated environment.

2) HSM vendors / certifications:
- Hosted: AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 depending on region) for envelope key material; primary key operations performed inside HSM.
- Dedicated: Option for AWS Nitro Enclaves + CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3).
- Private/on-prem: Customer-managed HSMs supported (Thales, Utimaco, YubiHSM for appliance options).
- Attestations: we maintain and can share FIPS attestation docs and third-party audit artifacts (see fips-attestation-2025.pdf).

3) Rotation policy:
- Data encryption keys (DEKs) used for per-object encryption are rotated by default every 90 days; rotation is automatic and seamless (older ciphertext remains readable via key version metadata).
- CMK rotation: we recommend an annual rotation for CMKs; Redwood supports automatic CMK rotation or manual rotation initiated by the customer. When using external KMS, rotation is controlled by the customer's KMS policy.
- Customers can configure custom cryptoperiods via the Redwood Console or API (supported in Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

4) Backups / snapshots:
- All persistent snapshots and backups are encrypted with envelope DEKs which are themselves encrypted under the CMK. Backups do not store unwrapped customer plaintext keys.
- Backup keys are not stored in plaintext alongside backups; key metadata and wrapped DEKs are stored in our encrypted config store with HSM-wrapped protection.

5) TLS and transport security:
- Minimum TLS version: TLS 1.2 (1.3 preferred); TLS 1.3 enabled by default on public endpoints.
- Cipher policy: modern AEAD ciphers only (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE with P-256/P-384).
- Mutual TLS: available for Dedicated and Private control planes and supported for customer-facing admin endpoints (mTLS using customer-provided client certs).
- Inter-node traffic in Dedicated/Private is mTLS by default; Hosted inter-service traffic is encrypted with mTLS within our service mesh and tenant isolation is enforced at the application and key layers.

Operational notes: audit logs (access to key material, key usage events) are retained and exportable; logs do not contain unencrypted customer plaintext. We can provide time-bounded audit export (S3/secure transfer) for compliance reviews.

Attachments: redwood-kms-ops-2026.pdf (ops summary), fips-attestation-2025.pdf (attestation), dataflow-diagram.png

Let me know if you'd like a 30-min call to walk through any of this with Marissa (security) and Aditya (solutions).

Thanks Rishi — a couple quick clarifications from our side after reviewing your attachments:

A) For Hosted BYOK imports, can you confirm the root-of-trust — is it an HSM-generated key that you control, or is it derived from a hardware root that the cloud provider attests? We need the attestation chain (vendor, module ID) to map to our control 3.2.

B) On backups: do you support separate backup-only keys (so backups can be revoked independently) or is there a single CMK envelope per tenant?

C) Is there an option for split-key escrow (dual-control) so Finity can require two parties to authorize key usage for emergency export?

If you can answer in-line, that helps accelerate our matrix.

- Thirdlane security ops

Subject: Re: KMS operational controls questions for Finity RFP

Hi — quick answers inline below:

A) Root-of-trust and attestation chain:
- For Hosted imports that land in our HSM fleet, the root-of-trust is the cloud HSM module (e.g., AWS CloudHSM cluster module ID). We obtain vendor-provided attestation documents for the module and can share module serial/IDs under NDA. The envelope root key used by Redwood is HSM-generated and never exported; attestation chain ties to the HSM vendor. See fips-attestation-2025.pdf for a sample.

B) Backup-only keys:
- Yes — customers can opt into separate backup encryption keys. This is a per-tenant configuration: backups can be encrypted under a distinct CMK (backup-CMK) to enable independent revocation and access control. Default is single CMK for simplicity, but we frequently configure backup-CMKs for customers with stricter controls.

C) Split-key / dual-control:
- We support dual-control patterns via two approaches: (1) orchestration-level split (two-man approval workflow in the Redwood Console + audit gates) and (2) cryptographic split using external HSMs that support key-sharding / split import (e.g., Thales with HSM sharding APIs). We can coordinate a deployment where Finity's key shares are required for critical actions.

Next steps: if this matches your needs, I'll propose a short confidentiality NDA addendum so we can share module serials and a scoped attestation export. Otherwise we can schedule a 30-minute technical call — I put a booking link here: https://meetings.example.com/rishi/finity-kms-call

Cheers,
Rishi
